gaps.criterion: Every client-gated action is independently enforced server side
gaps.gap: THIS IS CLIENT-SIDE GATING ONLY, and it is the same gap already open as a5844a5e#AC2 - the two are one piece of work. The PDP exists and this task now consumes it, but no mutating route calls it, so every action the UI disables remains reachable by calling the API directly with a valid token: POST /api/leads, POST /api/leads/:id/route, /assign and /first-response, POST /api/routing-rules with its PATCH and DELETE, POST /api/sla/evaluate. A hidden or disabled button is not a security control and this task's own acceptance line says so. The criterion also asks for proof by a test that calls the endpoint DIRECTLY, which cannot be written until the enforcement exists. Closing it: apply a PDP check in the mutating handlers, refuse on deny, persist the decision reference with the write, and add a negative api_definition testCase per route asserting the refusal - at which point this criterion and a5844a5e#AC2 and #AC4 all close together. I flagged this before starting the task and was asked to proceed, so it is recorded rather than silently absorbed.

gaps.criterion: Permission matrix screen renders from live policy data, not a static table
gaps.gap: The GROUPING is live and derived: toMatrixRows builds every row from PDP verdicts, splitting permits from approval-gated actions into their own columns, and an empty result renders an explicit loading-failure message rather than a blank grid an administrator would read as 'nobody can do anything'. What is missing is the screen that mounts it - PermissionMatrix is a component with no route, so nothing in the app navigates to it yet, and the role list it takes has no live source because sdk-persona GET /api/personas is not reachable here. Closing this needs an /app/admin/permissions route, the roles fetched rather than passed in, and a Gherkin scenario reaching the screen.
